name: United States
summary: Dogs (CDC, since 1 Aug 2024) need a CDC Dog Import Form receipt, must be at least 6 months old and microchipped; dogs that were in a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country in the past 6 months have extra rabies paperwork and port rules. Cats have no federal USDA requirements, but state rules apply. Dogs from screwworm-affected regions also need a USDA screwworm certificate.
microchip: Dogs: required, readable by a universal scanner. For the high-risk-country routes it must be implanted before the rabies vaccine, or the vaccine is invalid. Cats: no federal requirement.
vaccinations: Dogs only in dog-rabies-free/low-risk countries in the past 6 months: no federal rabies certificate required (CDC recommends vaccination; states and airlines may require it).

Dogs in a CDC high-risk country in the past 6 months: valid rabies vaccination given at 12 weeks (84 days) of age or older, after the microchip. US-vaccinated dogs: a first vaccine must be at least 28 days old when the CDC certification form is completed.
Cats: no federal USDA/APHIS requirement. Many states require rabies vaccination.
rabies_titer: Only for foreign-vaccinated dogs from high-risk countries: serology at a CDC-approved lab, drawn at least 30 days after the first valid vaccine and at least 28 days before entry. It stays valid as long as vaccination doesn't lapse. Without a valid titer, the dog does a 28-day quarantine at a CDC-registered animal care facility.
documents: CDC Dog Import Form receipt for every dog. Free, online, one per dog. Low-risk route: receipt valid 6 months. High-risk routes: single entry on the listed date and port.

US-vaccinated dogs returning from a high-risk country: Certification of U.S.-issued Rabies Vaccination, completed in USDA's system by a USDA-accredited vet and endorsed by USDA BEFORE the dog leaves the US.

Foreign-vaccinated dogs from a high-risk country: Certification of Foreign Rabies Vaccination and Microchip, endorsed by an official government vet and completed no more than 30 days before travel; titer report; reservation at a CDC-registered animal care facility (exam and US revaccination on arrival).

Dogs from screwworm (NWS)-affected regions, including US dogs returning from Mexico: certificate signed by a full-time official government vet of the region (Mexico: a SENASICA-authorized vet may sign) stating the dog was inspected within 5 days of shipment and is free of screwworm. APHIS's affected list includes most of Central America, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Haiti, Jamaica, Trinidad and Tobago, Aruba and the UAE; Mexico is under a separate temporary restriction.
Dogs from FMD-affected countries: no document, but coat and bedding must be free of excess dirt or straw, bathe on arrival, and keep away from livestock for 5 days.
import_permit: None for personal pets. Dogs imported for resale or adoption have additional USDA APHIS Animal Care permit and health requirements.
quarantine: None for compliant dogs. Foreign-vaccinated high-risk-country dogs without a valid titer: 28 days at a CDC-registered facility. HAWAII (state rule): up to 120 days' quarantine unless the 5-Day-Or-Less program is met: 2 rabies vaccinations (latest at least 30 days before arrival), a passing FAVN with arrival at least 30 days after the test, tick treatment, and documents received at least 10 days before arrival. Hawaii certificates also need a New World screwworm statement.
timeline: Plan at least 1 week before travel for a dog from a low-risk country (CDC form, microchip). For a high-risk country, plan at least 2 months: microchip, rabies vaccine at 12 weeks or older, titer at least 30 days later, facility reservation at least 30 days before travel. Hawaii direct release: plan 3–4+ months, because FAVN results can take 1–2 months. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~7 days for a dog from the EU/UK or another low-risk country (CDC Dog Import Form, age 6+ months, microchip; cats: no federal paperwork). Dogs vaccinated abroad that were in a CDC high-risk country (e.g. UAE) need a CDC-approved titer at least 28 days before entry plus a facility reservation: plan 2+ months. Hawaii: 3-4+ months.
private_aviation: CDC rules apply equally to private and charter flights; the arrival airport must match the CDC Dog Import Form. Dogs from low-risk countries and US-vaccinated dogs returning from high-risk countries may use any airport, land border or seaport. FOREIGN-VACCINATED dogs that were in a CDC high-risk country in the past 6 months (list of 15 Apr 2026 includes the UAE, Qatar, Türkiye, Israel, Morocco, Thailand and South Africa; not Saudi Arabia, Mexico, Bahamas, Japan, Singapore or Hong Kong) may enter ONLY through an airport with a CDC-registered animal care facility: ATL, DFW, LAX, MIA, JFK (not Teterboro, Newark or LaGuardia), PHL, SEA, IAD (CDC list updated 1 Sep 2026). Some facilities (SEA, LAX) work cargo-only or prefer cargo. This rules out typical FBO airports such as Teterboro, Van Nuys or Opa-locka for Dubai-vaccinated dogs. Hawaii: HNL direct airport release 8:30 am-4:30 pm daily; neighbor-island arrivals need a permit 30 days ahead; HDOA does not address private aircraft, so contact the Animal Quarantine Station.
export: Leaving the US: a USDA-accredited vet issues the destination-specific health certificate, preferably in VEHCS, and APHIS endorses it. Most endorsements are digital, but some destinations still require an original ink signature and embossing; a few (e.g. Bermuda, Belize, El Salvador, Honduras) need no APHIS endorsement. Before taking a dog to a CDC high-risk country, get the USDA-endorsed Certification of U.S.-issued Rabies Vaccination; otherwise re-entry requires the foreign-vaccinated route.
authority: CDC Division of Global Migration Health (dogs); USDA APHIS Veterinary Services; state veterinarians (Hawaii Department of Agriculture & Biosecurity, Animal Quarantine Station)

name: Canada
summary: Personal pet dogs (8 months or older) and cats (3 months or older) need a valid rabies vaccination certificate in English or French from a licensed vet; there's no quarantine and no permit. Commercial dogs (resale, adoption, fostering, breeding, show, research) from CFIA's high-risk dog-rabies countries have been banned since 28 Sep 2022, until further notice.
microchip: Not specifically required by CFIA for personal pets. The certificate must clearly identify the animal.
vaccinations: Dogs and cats 3 months or older: valid certificate showing current rabies vaccination, issued in English or French by a licensed vet. The APHIS Canada page says the vaccination must be current within 3 years of import.
Alternatives to vaccination: proof the animal comes from a CFIA-recognized rabies-free country where it lived for the past 6 months, OR a rabies titer of at least 0.5 IU/ml.
Animals under 3 months: no rabies requirement (proof of age may be requested).

Personal dogs under 8 months travelling unaccompanied: also need a vet certificate issued within 72 hours of import (dog at least 8 weeks old, vaccinated for distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus and parainfluenza at 6 weeks or older).
rabies_titer: Optional alternative to vaccination: RNATT of at least 0.5 IU/ml (drawn at least 30 days, or 3–4 weeks for dogs, after any prior vaccination).
documents: Rabies vaccination certificate (English or French) identifying the animal, or a rabies-free-country certificate, or a titer result.
Unaccompanied personal dogs under 8 months: vet health certificate within 72 hours of import (no APHIS endorsement needed from the US).
Assistance dogs accompanying their user: not subject to import restrictions.
import_permit: Not required for personal pets. Commercial dogs under 8 months need CFIA import permits and kennel-of-origin and quarantine-facility conditions. Commercial dogs from high-risk countries are prohibited (no permits issued).
quarantine: None. Pet dogs from any country are not subject to post-import quarantine. An inspector may order vaccination at the owner's expense if the paperwork is deficient.
timeline: Plan at least 1 month before travel: rabies vaccine (no minimum wait is stated, but vaccine must be valid), certificate in English or French; for a titer route, add 30+ days. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~3 days for a pet already rabies-vaccinated (certificate in English/French). No permit, no titer.
restricted_breeds: None federally. Provincial or municipal rules apply (e.g. Ontario's pit bull ban), so check locally.
private_aviation: No CFIA rule specific to private aircraft found; pets are presented to CBSA at the arrival airport with the rabies certificate.
export: Leaving Canada: the destination's certificate is issued by a licensed vet and endorsed by CFIA where the destination requires it. Dogs going to the US follow CDC low-risk rules (Canada isn't a CDC high-risk country): CDC Dog Import Form, age 6 months or older, microchip.
authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA); border inspection by CBSA

name: Mexico
summary: From the US: cats need no health certificate (since 16 Dec 2019), but since 3 Aug 2026 dogs need an 'NWS Inspection Certificate for Pet Dogs' signed by a USDA-accredited vet no more than 5 days before entry (no APHIS endorsement). SENASICA (OISA) inspects all dogs and cats on arrival for disease signs, ectoparasites and wounds. Requirements for non-US origins were not verified.
vaccinations: No rabies certificate is listed as an entry requirement on the APHIS Mexico page (Sep 2026). Carry rabies proof anyway for the US return.
parasite_treatment: The pet must be free of ectoparasites at the SENASICA inspection. If ticks are found, they are sampled and removed, and the pet is held at OISA until cleared, at the importer's cost. Other ectoparasites must be treated by a vet of the owner's choice.
documents: Dogs: NWS (New World screwworm) Inspection Certificate for Pet Dogs, issued no more than 5 days before entry by a USDA-accredited vet. No APHIS endorsement. Don't list cats on the dog form, or the form becomes invalid.
Cats: none.
Carriers must be clean; bedding, toys and food beyond the arrival day are removed.
import_permit: Not required for personal pets. A 'Pet Program – Frequent Traveler' registration is available.
timeline: Plan at least 1 week before travel: book a USDA-accredited vet for the NWS inspection within 5 days of the flight; arrange the Mexican-side screwworm certificate for the return to the US. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~7 days from the USA: NWS inspection certificate for dogs within 5 days before entry (no endorsement). Cats: none. Non-US origins not verified.
private_aviation: No private-aviation specifics are published. SENASICA/OISA inspects at the point of entry, so confirm with the FBO and handler that SENASICA inspection is available at the arrival airport and time.
export: Returning or entering the US from Mexico: dogs need a screwworm-freedom certificate. For Mexico, a SENASICA-authorized clinical vet (MVRA directory) may sign it, with inspection within 5 days. Mexico is NOT on the CDC high-risk list, so the CDC Dog Import Form route applies.
authority: SENASICA (Servicio Nacional de Sanidad, Inocuidad y Calidad Agroalimentaria), OISA inspection offices

name: Bahamas
summary: Get a BAHFSA veterinary import permit (e-permitting, apply at least 4 weeks ahead) and a USDA-accredited vet export health certificate issued within 10 days of export. Dogs must be 6 months or older, ISO-microchipped before rabies vaccination, and not a banned breed. From 1 Jan 2027, US certificates must be electronically endorsed by APHIS.
microchip: ISO-compliant microchip required (dogs), implanted before the rabies vaccination.
vaccinations: Rabies (dogs): most recent vaccine given at 12 weeks or older. 1-year vaccine: no less than 1 month and no more than 10 months before import. 3-year vaccine: no less than 1 month and no more than 34 months before import.
Dogs: distemper, parvovirus, leptospirosis, hepatitis and parainfluenza, at least 10 days before export.
parasite_treatment: Within 10 days before export: external parasite treatment and a broad-spectrum internal dewormer (licensed in the US).
documents: BAHFSA veterinary import permit.

US export health certificate for pet dogs or cats (VEHCS forms dated Sep 2026). Inspection within 10 days before export. Includes New World screwworm statements if the animal comes from an APHIS-defined NWS-infested zone.
From 1 Jan 2027: electronically signed by the accredited vet AND electronically endorsed by APHIS.
import_permit: Required. Apply through the Bahamas Agricultural Health and Food Safety Authority (BAHFSA) e-permitting portal at least 4 weeks before travel.
timeline: Plan at least 5-6 weeks before travel: check the rabies vaccine window, apply for the BAHFSA permit at least 4 weeks ahead, then do the vet exam, deworming and tick treatment within 10 days before departure, and the APHIS endorsement. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~30 days from the USA: BAHFSA permit at least 4 weeks ahead; exam and parasite treatments within 10 days. Requirements from EU origin were not verified (sources are US-based).
restricted_breeds: Prohibited (including crosses): Pit Bull, Presa Canario, Cane Corso, American Bully, Dogo Argentino, Staffordshire Terrier.
private_aviation: BAHFSA conditions for other regulated animals (Sep 2026) require 24 hours' notice of arrival to Veterinary Services and a separate inspection fee for landings after 5 pm Mon–Fri, on weekends or on public holidays. Confirm the same applies to dogs and cats when the permit is issued.
authority: Bahamas Agricultural Health and Food Safety Authority (BAHFSA), Veterinary Services Unit

name: Cayman Islands
summary: A Department of Agriculture import permit is needed. Pets need an ISO microchip, rabies vaccination per Cayman guidelines and, unless coming from a 'no rabies-risk' territory, a FAVN titer: 'low-risk' origins (US mainland, Canada) may enter no sooner than 2 months after the blood draw, 'high-risk' origins (e.g. Mexico, Puerto Rico, Dominican Republic) 3 months. 'No-risk' territories include the UK, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, Netherlands, Portugal, Greece, Monaco, Bahamas, Barbados, Australia and New Zealand. No quarantine option: non-compliant pets are returned or destroyed. No direct imports from Asia (incl. UAE), Africa, or Central/South America.
microchip: ISO-compliant 15-digit chip if implanted on or after 1 Mar 2019 (older chips: 10 or more characters), implanted BEFORE rabies vaccination, otherwise revaccinate. Scanned at each step.
vaccinations: Rabies: first vaccine at 12 weeks or older; booster 9–12 months later; 2- or 3-year intervals only after that second dose. Valid for entry 30 days after vaccination for 'no-risk' origins.
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis and parvovirus mandatory. Cats: panleukopenia, herpesvirus and calicivirus mandatory.
rabies_titer: Required unless coming from a 'no rabies-risk' territory (official 2026 list includes e.g. UK, Ireland, France, Germany, Italy, Spain incl. Balearics/Canaries, Portugal, Greece, Netherlands, Belgium, Switzerland, Monaco, Austria, Bahamas, Barbados, Bermuda, Jamaica, Hawaii, Australia, New Zealand). Blood drawn at least 30 days after vaccination at a Cayman-approved lab, result at least 0.5 IU/ml with the microchip number, repeated every 12 months. Earliest entry after the draw: 2 months for 'low risk' origins (US mainland, Canada, Bulgaria, Croatia, Hungary, Latvia, Estonia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Grenada, Trinidad & Tobago) and 3 months for 'high risk' origins (e.g. Mexico, Puerto Rico, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Haiti, Poland, Romania, Lithuania, Serbia, Montenegro, Greenland). Pets must have resided in the origin country for at least 3 months. Animals arriving by sea are treated as high risk.
parasite_treatment: On the day of the vet examination, within 14 days before travel: praziquantel at 5 mg/kg (tapeworm) plus a systemic tick product with residual action. Shampoos, collars and flea-only products are not accepted.
documents: Cayman Islands import permit (single entry, valid 14 days from the health-certificate exam date).

Veterinary health certificate completed within 14 days of travel. The new US VEHCS certificate (Sep 2026) includes a USDA endorsement block, and APHIS indicates endorsement applies from 1 Oct 2026; previously Cayman needed no APHIS endorsement for dogs and cats. Original presented on arrival.
FAVN report, rabies and routine vaccination certificates, signed breed declaration and full-body colour photo (dogs).
import_permit: Required. Email the application and documents to ci.agriculturevs@gov.ky, up to 6 months before travel. Fee CI$50 / US$61 per animal. Decision within 3 working days of a complete file. The health certificate must be added within 14 days before entry.
quarantine: None available. Non-compliant animals are refused and returned immediately, or destroyed, at the importer's expense. Dogs staying more than 30 days must be licensed.
timeline: Plan at least 3 months (US mainland) or 4 months (higher-risk origins) before travel: microchip, then rabies vaccine, then FAVN at least 30 days later, then wait 2–3 months; apply for the permit; vet exam and treatments within 14 days of travel; give 48 hours' notice of arrival. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~65 days from the US mainland (titer blood draw on a currently vaccinated pet, then 2 months' wait). From 'no-risk' EU countries or the UK: ~3 weeks (permit, exam and treatments within 14 days). From the UAE: not possible directly (must route via a non-Asian country).
restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Pit Bull Terrier types, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, and dogs bred for fighting. Crosses are allowed only if spayed or neutered (proof required) and not pregnant. Purebreds not originating in Cayman are never admitted.
private_aviation: Travel by the most direct route. No animal may be imported DIRECTLY from Asia (including the UAE/Dubai), Africa, or Central or South America. Transit through such a country requires a government-sealed crate. Give 48 hours' notice of arrival time and flight. DoA office hours are Mon–Fri 8:30 am–5:00 pm, so confirm inspector availability for FBO arrivals outside these hours.
export: Leaving Cayman: DoA export permit/health certificate (fee CI$20 / US$25 per animal). Pets abroad for less than 14 days can re-enter on the export certificate plus a tick and tapeworm treatment.
authority: Cayman Islands Department of Agriculture – Veterinary Services

name: Barbados
summary: Get an import permit first (valid 6 months). Pets need an ISO microchip, rabies vaccination with a 35-day wait after a primary dose, and, if in a Category 2 country within 3 months or arriving by sea, a FAVN. Dogs need heartworm and tick/tapeworm treatment. An officially endorsed certificate within 7 days of travel is required, plus 3 working days' notice. The US is Category 1.
microchip: ISO 11784 / ISO 11785 Annex A microchip, implanted before or at the time of rabies vaccination.
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated vaccine, first dose at 3 months or older. Wait 35 days after a primary vaccination, or after revaccination following a lapse (vaccination day = day 0). Boosters on or before the expiry date.
rabies_titer: Required only for pets in a Category 2 country within the 3 months before travel (Category 1 = rabies-free or low risk; the US is Category 1) and for all sea arrivals. Blood drawn at an approved lab at least 30 days after vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml. Pets must have spent 3 continuous months in Category 1 countries to use the Category 1 route.
parasite_treatment: Dogs only: ticks plus tapeworm (praziquantel) within 7 days before leaving. Heartworm test (dogs over 6 months) within 30 days, ELISA antigen; Knott's test if positive or previously treated. Cats: none.
documents: Barbados import permit (Veterinary Services, Ministry of Agriculture), valid 6 months.
Official export health certificate: exam within 7 days of travel, endorsed by an official government vet (APHIS digital endorsement via VEHCS). Valid 10 days from endorsement.
Customs broker (required); airline 'Pre-Alert' listing the animals.
import_permit: Required, obtained FIRST from Veterinary Services, Barbados. Valid 6 months from issue.
timeline: Plan at least 2 months before travel (US-origin): permit, microchip and rabies (35-day wait), heartworm test within 30 days, vet exam and treatments within 7 days, APHIS endorsement, 3 working days' notice. From Category 2 countries (e.g. UAE), add the FAVN step. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~21 days from the USA (Category 1) if the rabies vaccine is more than 35 days old: permit, heartworm test within 30 days, exam and dog treatments within 7 days, endorsement, 3 working days' notice. Category 2 origins (e.g. UAE) add a FAVN.
private_aviation: Give at least 3 working days' notice of arrival (246-427-5492 / 427-5073, vetservices@caribsurf.com) with the owner, customs broker and flight details. Animals go directly from the aircraft to the Animal Reception Centre; cabin pets are handed to handling agents, and customs treats pets as cargo. Government hours are Mon–Fri 8:15 am–4:30 pm; arrivals outside these hours, on weekends or on holidays incur overtime inspection fees. Effect for private jets: even a cabin pet is treated as cargo and handed over for veterinary and customs clearance through a customs broker.
authority: Veterinary Services Department, Ministry of Agriculture, Food, Fisheries and Water Resource Management, Barbados

name: United Kingdom (Great Britain and Northern Ireland)
summary: Great Britain: microchip, rabies vaccination (21-day wait), correct document (EU pet passport, GB AHC or GB pet health certificate), tapeworm treatment for dogs, entry only via an approved route/carrier (no route needed from Ireland/within UK); unlisted countries also need a titer test and 3-month wait. Northern Ireland follows EU rules (see notes).
microchip: Microchip before (or at the same time as) rabies vaccination; otherwise revaccination needed.
vaccinations: Rabies: pet >=12 weeks; wait at least 21 full days after the first vaccination (or last dose of primary course); boosters within validity need no wait.
rabies_titer: Great Britain: required only from unlisted countries (not EU and not listed): sample >=30 days after vaccination, EU-approved lab, >=0.5 IU/ml, wait 3 months from sample date; exception if vaccinated, tested and documented in the EU before going to the unlisted country. Northern Ireland: same (Category 3 = unlisted).
parasite_treatment: Dogs: tapeworm (Echinococcus) treatment by a vet not less than 24 hours and not more than 5 days before arrival in GB (not needed for dogs coming directly from Ireland, Finland, Malta, Northern Ireland or Norway - per EU equivalence; confirm on gov.uk tapeworm page). Northern Ireland: dogs 24-120 h before arrival; not required from Republic of Ireland.
documents: GB from EU: EU pet passport, or GB AHC issued within previous 6 months, or GB pet health certificate (or GB pet passport issued before 1 Jan 2021).
GB from listed non-EU countries: GB pet health certificate (some listed territories, e.g. AD, IS, NO, CH, GI, also accept pet passport/AHC).
GB from unlisted countries: GB pet health certificate + rabies blood test result.
Pet travel declaration (non-commercial).
From Northern Ireland, Channel Islands, Isle of Man: no pet passport or health certificate needed for GB.
More than 5 pets (not for event), pet travelling >5 days apart from owner, or sale/rehoming: Balai commercial import rules.

NORTHERN IRELAND: from GB, UK-resident pets can use the NI Pet Travel Scheme (free NI Pet Travel Document + declaration not to travel on to EU); otherwise EU rules - EU pet passport or AHC (10 days from issue for entry); Part 2 listed countries (incl. GB not using NIPTS) and unlisted countries must enter via a Travellers' Point of Entry.
quarantine: None if compliant. Non-compliant pets may be quarantined for up to 4 months (or refused entry if arriving by sea), at owner's expense.
timeline: EU/listed origin: at least 4 weeks (microchip -> rabies at >=12 weeks -> 21 days -> document -> dog tapeworm 1-5 days before). Unlisted origin: at least 4 months (add blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then 3-month wait). Book an approved carrier/route before travel. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~10 days from the USA or EU (listed countries): GB pet health certificate (or EU pet passport / AHC), dog tapeworm 1-5 days before arrival, and an approved charter operator booked for the arrival airport.
restricted_breeds: Banned types (by appearance): Pit Bull Terrier, Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, XL Bully. Cannot be brought into GB without a valid Certificate of Exemption. Northern Ireland has its own XL Bully rules.
private_aviation: GREAT BRITAIN: pets normally must travel as cargo by air, EXCEPT on a chartered private plane, but only with operators on the APHA 'approved air routes - charter airlines' list for the specific arrival airport (pets carried in the cabin). Charter-listed GB airports include Biggin Hill, Farnborough, London Luton, London Stansted, London Gatwick, London Heathrow, London Oxford, Blackbushe, Birmingham, Manchester, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Bristol, Cambridge, Cardiff, Bournemouth, Southampton, Liverpool, Newcastle, Leeds Bradford, East Midlands, Lydd, Blackpool, Gloucestershire, Humberside, Sheffield, often via named pet-check providers. Northolt, Doncaster and Prestwick are NOT on the list (gov.uk list updated 9 Oct 2026). No approved route needed from Ireland or within the UK. Verify the operator/airport pairing on gov.uk before each flight. NORTHERN IRELAND: air points of entry Belfast International, Belfast City, City of Derry; for air arrivals notify DAERA at least 10 days before travel (daeratradeimports@daera-ni.gov.uk).
export: Great Britain to EU (and to Northern Ireland outside NIPTS): Animal Health Certificate (AHC) issued by an Official Veterinarian, new AHC for each trip, used within 10 days of issue for EU entry; then valid 6 months for onward EU travel and re-entry to GB (if rabies vaccination stays valid). EU pet passports issued in GB cannot be used by GB residents to enter the EU. Northern Ireland residents can use EU pet passports. Max 5 pets in a private vehicle unless for events.
authority: Defra / Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) - Great Britain; DAERA - Northern Ireland

name: France
summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131, documents Reg. 2026/705, listed countries Reg. 2026/636): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test with 3-month wait if the country is unlisted), presented to French Customs on arrival. Category 1 attack dogs are banned outright, even in transit. Imported dogs must have at least one adult tooth.
microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO 11784/11785-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU. Per the DGAL note (June 2026) listing the titer-exempt countries of Reg. (EU) 2026/636, the following are NOT listed, so pets coming from them need the titer + 3-month wait: Türkiye, Morocco, Israel, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Thailand, South Africa, Maldives, Bahamas (Mexico, Barbados, Cayman Islands, Malaysia and Taiwan ARE listed; Russia and Belarus were removed in 2024).
parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 (Annex IV) model remain acceptable until 31 Mar 2027 if issued before 1 Oct 2026 (DGAL note, June 2026).
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.

Young animals: this country does NOT accept unvaccinated/insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under ~15 weeks) from other EU states; never allowed from third countries. (French Customs: dogs under 16 weeks are not admitted.)
quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~10 days from the USA (EU-listed country; pet already chipped and rabies-vaccinated more than 21 days ago): EU animal health certificate issued and government-endorsed (USDA APHIS) within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From an unlisted country without a prior titer: ~100+ days.
restricted_breeds: Category 1 (attack dogs, import banned, including in transit): dogs of Staffordshire Terrier / American Staffordshire Terrier ('pit-bull'), Mastiff ('boerbull') or Tosa type WITHOUT registration in a recognised pedigree book. Category 2 (import allowed with proof of pedigree registration; leash, muzzle and owner obligations apply): pedigree Staffordshire Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier and Tosa, and ALL Rottweilers or Rottweiler-type dogs with or without pedigree. Bengal and Savannah cats without proof of breed (pedigree/birth certificate) are treated as hybrids and need a prior import permit from the regional DREAL. Wolf-dog hybrids likewise. Any dog imported from a third country must have at least one adult tooth (Code rural L236-1), which in practice excludes very young puppies.
private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories such as CH, MC, AD, GI, IS, LI, SM, VA, FO, GL and Northern Ireland) must present the pet to French Customs (red channel/'filtre') for documentary and identity checks before leaving the international zone; no appointment is needed. Le Bourget (LFPB) and Nice (LFMN): France has no published airport-by-airport list in the official sources retrieved. The DGAL note (June 2026) states customs carry out these checks 'aux points ouverts au trafic international de voyageurs', and the Ministry of Agriculture's guidance says pets from third countries are checked by customs 'at all passenger entry points'.
